title: Quantile-driven headroom sampler with deferred enrichment
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Reduce runtime tracing overhead while preserving high-fidelity tail analysis by introducing a quantile-driven headroom sampling controller paired with deferred enrichment (post-retention span hydration). The controller maintains minimal hotpath work: a tiny per-request headroom score computed with an exponential moving quantile estimate and a lightweight deterministic sampling decision. For retained traces we schedule an async enrichment job that merges high-cardinality metadata (e.g., request body, stack snapshots, full headers) and writes the enriched trace to the sink.

Objectives: (1) cut median hotpath tracing CPU/allocs by >40% across inference services, (2) keep 99th-percentile tail capture fidelity comparable to today for routes flagged as high-visibility, and (3) provide clear SLOs and metrics for sampling-induced blindspots so alerts drive rollbacks or increased retention automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath: per-request tracing overhead (allocs + CPU) is reduced by >=40% in benchmarked inference worker under representative QPS profile
Tail fidelity: for top-50 high-visibility routes, the proportion of tail incidents (p99 latency spikes or errors) captured by retained traces remains >=95% compared to full-trace baseline
Operational controls: runtime flags to toggle controller mode (off / conservative / aggressive) and per-route override via console exist
Deferred enrichment: enrichment jobs complete within configured window (default 30s) and do not add back hotpath overhead
Observability: dashboards for sampling rate, enrichment lag, p99 retention coverage, and sampling-induced false-negative incidents are added and instrumented into alerting
Graceful rollout: canary on 5% of traffic with automatic rollback on enrichment-lag > 3x SLA or tail-coverage drop below threshold
rollout_plan: Phase A: feature-flagged deploy to a small staging fleet with synthetic tail traffic profile. Phase B: canary 5% of production traffic for non-critical routes (72h), measure enrichment lag and tail-coverage. Phase C: expand to 25% with conservative mode, collect metrics for 1 week. Phase D: enable per-route overrides for top 50 routes and move to default conservative mode unless route owner opts in. Rollback triggers: enrichment lag > 10s for >1% of retained traces OR p99 retention coverage < 90% for flagged routes. Document rollout notes in confluence and announce to platform-oncall and route owners.
testing_plan: Unit tests for quantile estimator and deterministic sampler (edge cases, overflow, seed stability)
Integration tests simulating bursty tail workloads and verifying enrichment jobs attach expected metadata
Load test comparing hotpath CPU/allocs with and without headroom sampler using our perf harness (script: perf/tracing/headroom-endpoint)
Chaos test: simulate enrichment worker failures and validate backpressure/backoff and metrics emission
Canary asserts: automated job to compute p50/p95/p99 retention coverage against baseline traces during canary window
